chapter: Newark and first years in Harlem
title: Harlem wonderland: the Rhythm Club and Jelly Roll Morton's audition
summary: Living on Edgecombe Avenue, he haunted the Rhythm Club among Harlem's stars, and Jelly Roll Morton had him read music on the spot and told him to return at eight.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Remembering Jelly Roll Morton: the man, the band

blocks.x: So I started living on Edgecombe Avenue) and I was living right across the street from one of my aunts and didn't know it. She didn't know it either, so now I'm here in this big city as you said, and I'm seeing lights and guys are going through the Tree of Hope and I'm meeting these big stars. I was going to a place called the Rhythm Club, Jelly Roll Morton, Fletcher Henderson, Coleman Hawkins, and Elmer Williams, and Rex Stewart -- by the way, he's from Washington and I'm meeting these and Ovie Alston and Sandy Williams, these people. I even seen Henry Goodman, I haven't seen these people. These people at this time they're wearing tight pants and velvet coats and Metcalfe had a Cadillac and -- Bojangles and all these stars, and these pretty ladies, oh, my goodness. I was really in wonderland, so then all right, (unintelligible) so Jelly Roll Morton says look, what you doing around here. I said, sir, I would like to have a job and he said, do you

read music. Yes, sir. Where you come from anyway (unintelligible) no, sir, I come from Lafayette, Louisiana. Can you read music. Yes, sir, well, go and get it. This is 12 o'clock in the day. I got my tuxedo and put it on. Read that. I read it.
At the Rhythm Club in front of everybody. Read that. So I read it. He said, go home and take your tuxedo off and then come back at 8 o'clock here. Yes, sir.
